=== DOCS-TRUTH (verified 2026-06-08 via WebFetch trino.io/docs/467/connector/iceberg.html) ===

• **Time travel:** Trino 467 supports BOTH `FOR VERSION AS OF <snapshot_id>` (BIGINT or branch/tag name string) and `FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF TIMESTAMP '...'` (TIMESTAMP/DATE literal). Docs example verbatim: `SELECT * FROM example.testdb.customer_orders FOR VERSION AS OF 8954597067493422955` and `SELECT * FROM example.testdb.customer_orders FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF TIMESTAMP '2022-03-23 09:59:29.803 Europe/Vienna'`.
• **Metadata tables:** `$snapshots`, `$history`, `$files`, `$manifests`, `$partitions`, `$refs`, `$properties`, `$entries`, `$all_entries` — all exposed on Trino 467. Access requires double-quoted `"<table>$<metadata>"` form due to `$` not being a valid unquoted identifier character.
• **Rollback (Trino 467):** ONLY `CALL <catalog>.system.rollback_to_snapshot(<schema_varchar>, <table_varchar>, <snapshot_id_bigint>)` — positional three-arg form. Docs example: `CALL example.system.rollback_to_snapshot('testdb', 'customer_orders', 8954597067493422955)`. The `ALTER TABLE ... EXECUTE rollback_to_snapshot(...)` form does NOT exist in Trino 467 — Trino 467's ALTER TABLE EXECUTE procedures are limited to optimize / expire_snapshots / remove_orphan_files / drop_extended_stats. The EXECUTE rollback form was added in Trino 469 (released Jan 2025) per trinodb/trino #24580. Do NOT cross the syntaxes: Trino 467 = CALL positional; Trino 469+ = ALTER TABLE EXECUTE positional bigint; Spark = CALL with `table => 'schema.table'` single-qualified-string + `snapshot_id => ...` named args.
• **Partition evolution:** `ALTER TABLE <table> SET PROPERTIES partitioning = ARRAY[<transforms>]` — applies to NEW writes only; existing files keep their old partition layout; Trino reads transparently across mixed specs. SET PARTITION SPEC / ADD PARTITION FIELD / REPLACE PARTITION FIELD are Spark-dialect ONLY, NOT Trino 467.
• **CTAS with partitioning:** `CREATE TABLE <name> WITH (partitioning = ARRAY['<transform>', ...]) AS SELECT ...`. Each transform is a SINGLE-quoted STRING inside ARRAY[...] inside WITH (...). bucket() is COLUMN-FIRST: `bucket(col, N)` in Trino (vs Spark's bucket(N, col)).

=== EDIT (ONE; REPLACE-in-place; verified-false claim fixed) ===

**resources/27-oracle-plsql-to-dbt-trino.md line 4122** — fixed verified-false claim presenting the Trino 469+ ALTER TABLE EXECUTE rollback form as the (unqualified) "Trino" way for the dbt + Trino-on-Iceberg ROLLBACK-semantics card.

• **BEFORE:** `- **Iceberg snapshot rollback** for "I committed bad data, restore the previous snapshot." Trino: \`ALTER TABLE my_table EXECUTE rollback_to_snapshot(<previous_snapshot_id>)\`. This rolls the table back to a prior known-good state. See [resource 17 § Iceberg time travel and rollback](17-iceberg-table-maintenance.md).`

• **AFTER:** `- **Iceberg snapshot rollback** for "I committed bad data, restore the previous snapshot." **On Trino 467 (our production version), the ONLY valid rollback syntax is \`CALL iceberg.system.rollback_to_snapshot('schema', 'table', <previous_snapshot_id>)\`** — positional VARCHAR, VARCHAR, BIGINT three-arg form. Verified at [trino.io/docs/467/connector/iceberg.html](https://trino.io/docs/467/connector/iceberg.html) (docs example: \`CALL example.system.rollback_to_snapshot('testdb', 'customer_orders', 8954597067493422955)\`). The \`ALTER TABLE <table> EXECUTE rollback_to_snapshot(<id>)\` table-procedure form was added in **Trino 469** (Jan 2025) and does **NOT** exist on Trino 467 — pasting it returns a procedure-not-found / parse error. This rolls the table back to a prior known-good state. See [resource 17 § Iceberg time travel and rollback](17-iceberg-table-maintenance.md) for the full canonical-forms card and the Trino-vs-Spark rollback syntax matrix.`
